The announcement drew criticism from Nato's chief military analyst, General John Allen, who said the move could provoke "battling on the defensive". He wrote that the US and its allies were "more than capable of taking such measures with a sense of urgency and with the requisite force" but that they had to do so at a time when they were concerned about the security of their allies. "The US and its allies are far more capable of threatening NATO, its allies are far more capable of taking such measures with a sense of urgency and with the requisite force in a situation of war, because it is much more difficult for them to achieve it without being exposed to the consequences," he wrote.
